title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency: Days Charged in the New Room after a Mid-Month Move
content:
**Admissions and billing guidance — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** The new room's span days — the days the new-room span charges — follow the credits on the advance charge the span is split from.

| What the old room's advance charge shows | New room's span days |
|---|---|
| A room-change credit | The days that credit takes off, from its first credited day |
| No room-change credit, and the agreement records the move before the first day of that charge's span | From the first day of the span through its last day |
| No room-change credit, and the move is recorded on or after the span's first day | From the move date recorded on the agreement through the last day of the span, both days included |

A move the resident requests reprices from the move date, save that a requested move into a tier whose daily rate under the current private pay schedule is higher than that of the tier the resident left, where the resident's latest room-change request was logged on or before the move date recorded on the agreement and names a later date inside the span of the advance charge billed for the room the resident left, reprices from that requested date, the resident not being charged the higher rate before the date asked for, and both the room-change credit on that advance and the new room's span reprice from it; every other move reprices from the move date.

**Hypothetical cases.** A room-change credit of 11 days from the 20th day of a 30-day span: the new room's span days are days 20 to 30. A move recorded three days before a 30-day span begins and no credit on it: all 30 days.
